semantic_claims.text: Hi! Let's count Fibonacci numbers, and watch each new number take shape.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Introduces Fibonacci counting and arithmetic generation; no biological or spiral claim.

semantic_claims.text: We start with zero and one. These are our two starting values.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Two initial terms are assigned0 and1; neither is presented as a result of the n>=2 recurrence.

semantic_claims.text: To make the next number, add the previous two. Then use the newest pair, and do it again.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Previous two terms produce the next; pair update is (F[n-2],F[n-1])->(F[n-1],F[n]).

semantic_claims.text: The small labels tell us each number's place. We start at F zero, so F two is the third entry.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: F0 is entry1, F1 entry2, F2 entry3. F2 value is1, not2.

semantic_claims.text: The older value sits on the left. The newer value sits beside it. Their labels move with them.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: The older/newer operand order is F[n-2] on the left and F[n-1] beside it, matching every state.

semantic_claims.text: Listen for plus and equals. The answer appears when we say its name, and becomes our newest value.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Plus and equals mark addition; the output becomes the new member of the next pair. Display anticipates its voice by0.12s; this is a presentation lead, not a different mathematical value.

semantic_claims.text: Number windows show values, not piles of things. A window marked one thousand stands for that value, not one thousand objects.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Number windows are symbols for values;1000 does not claim1000 pictured objects. Small-dot diagrams and large symbolic values are not equated.

semantic_claims.text: We'll keep adding until the sequence first passes one hundred million. The numbers grow, but the rule stays the same.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: F40=102334155 is the first term above100000000. General growth wording does not assert strict growth at the repeated1; the duplicate is explicitly explained.

semantic_claims.text: There are two ones in a row. One is a starting value; the next was made by adding zero and one.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: F1=1 is a seed; F2=0+1=1 is generated. Two adjacent ones have different indices.

semantic_claims.text: They have the same value, but different places. Keep both entries, because each belongs to the sequence.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Equal values can occupy distinct sequence positions. Removing one would break the recurrence/indexing.

semantic_claims.text: Let's look inside that addition. In the ones column, eight plus three makes eleven: one stays here, and one ten moves left.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: 8+13: ones8+3=11, keep1one and carry1ten.

semantic_claims.text: That carried ten joins the ten already there. The columns now show two tens and one one. Then the newest pair moves on.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Existing1ten plus carried1ten gives2tens; two tens and one one denotes20+1=21, not201 or211.

semantic_claims.text: Here the ones make thirteen. Write three and carry one ten. The tens, including that carry, also make thirteen.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: 89+144: ones9+4=13; tens8+4+1=13, including the first carry.

semantic_claims.text: Write three tens, and carry one hundred. That hundred joins the hundred already there. Every column keeps its own place.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Write3tens and carry1hundred; that carried100 joins the original100 in144, giving2hundreds. Repeated hundred noun mentions refer to the same carry/units, not extra independent additions.

semantic_claims.text: Now the values reach into the thousands. Start at the ones and follow each carry to the next column, one place at a time.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: This checkpoint is already in the thousands; it does not claim F18 is the first four-digit term (F17 is1597). Right-to-left column processing is correct.

semantic_claims.text: Seven plus seven makes fourteen. Next come eighteen tens, then fifteen hundreds. Each carry moves one column left; it never skips a place.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: 987+1597:7+7=14, then8+9+1=18tens, then9+5+1=15hundreds, then0+1+1=2thousands. Carry moves to the adjacent next place.

semantic_claims.text: The commas help us read groups of three digits. They are separators, not extra digits, and they do not change the addition.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Commas separate groups from the right every3digits; the leftmost group may contain1–3digits. The statement does not claim commas add a digit.

semantic_claims.text: Keep the ones columns lined up on the right. Even with larger numbers, each column still adds the same kind of units.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Ones alignment means equal place values share a column, and each column adds like units.

semantic_claims.text: We have reached the final pair for this journey. Both values are below one hundred million. Their sum will cross that mark.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: The final pair means F38=39088169 and F39=63245986. Both are below100million and their sum102334155 is above. The renderer last-pair replay explicitly draws equation index40, not the earlier F37+F38 calculation.

semantic_claims.text: Watch the labels as the two values enter the formula. It is the same addition we used at the start, with more place-value columns.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Same recurrence applied to the last pair with more place columns, without changing its arithmetic meaning.

semantic_claims.text: We've counted forty-one entries, from F zero through F forty. Two starting values, then thirty-nine additions brought us here.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: Indices0through40 inclusive give41terms. Two seeds plus39recurrence evaluations give41entries.

semantic_claims.text: The newest number is just past one hundred million. We stop here today, but the rule can keep making more numbers.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: 102334155 exceeds100million by2334155 (2.334155%). Stopping is an editorial choice; the recurrence can continue.

semantic_claims.text: Remember the motion: take the previous two, add them, keep the newest pair, and repeat. Every new entry has a place in the chain.
semantic_claims.semantic_review: State update retains the newest pair and repeats; every entry has its own index, without requiring all values to be distinct.
